correctness.rationale: Correct motion-invariant measure is dσ(u)ds conditioned on hitting the body, not uniform normals after conditioning. Each generic plane intersects three or four tetrahedral edges; integrate the six |u⋅edge| crossing intervals to obtain E N=2π Σ ℓ_e/(Σ ℓ_e θ_e), with exterior dihedral θ_e and polyhedral mean-width identity. For T_t, Σℓ=L=2+t+2sqrt(1+t²)+sqrt2 and Σℓ θ=(π/2)L+2sqrt(1+t²)atan(t/sqrt(1+t²))+sqrt2 atan(1/(sqrt2 t)), yielding P=4/(1+2D/(πL))-3. Differentiating R=D/L gives sign(A/B-G(t)); A/B is strictly increasing, G strictly decreasing and they meet at t=1, proving strict ascent/decline, the unique maximum P(1)=0.2532844262756413, boundary limits 3-2sqrt2 and 0, and exact inverse multiplicities. Independent 3×30,000-direction Crofton quadrature independently integrates widths/crossing contributions and verifies five-parameter monotonicity; finite quadrature is corroboration only.
residual_risks: The proof uses exterior dihedral angles and width-biased conditional normals; replacing them with interior angles/uniform normals invalidates the formula.
Finite quadrature does not establish derivative sign globally.
